subject: Mutual Action Plan — technical evaluation milestone: scope, owners & target dates
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan — technical evaluation milestone: scope, owners & target dates

Hi Sara / Ben —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Short recap and proposed next steps tied to the MAP milestone we discussed (Technical evaluation / benchmarks). Please review and confirm owners & timelines so we can lock the test window.

1) Objective (what success looks like)
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for 128-token generation on Dedicated capacity during steady-state testing.
- Throughput: sustain >= 25 qps for concurrent short-text completions (avg 64 tokens).
- Quality: pass accuracy/regression checks vs your 150-key prompt set (>= 92% pass on Critical paths; False-positive tolerances defined in the shared doc).
- Unit cost: target <= $0.03 per 1k tokens for production run (benchmarks will measure realized token cost on our infra).

2) Proposed model shortlist (for the benchmark runs)
- Redwood-1 (13B, optimized int8 path)
- Llama3-7B (q4f16 quantized)
- Mistral-7B (8-bit optimized)
- Fallback: partner GPT-4o endpoint (if a larger model is required for quality baseline)

3) Responsibilities (MAP owners)
- HealthGrid (Sara / Ben): provide representative prompt set (CSV) + 100 sample conversations, confirm acceptance criteria, and enable a test service account / VPC peering info or test endpoint.
- Redwood (Neha / Rishi / Eng): run benchmark harness, deliver latency/cost/quality report, and outline rollout guidance (quantization recommendations & batching).
- CS (Monica): coordinate procurement/testing schedule and ensure legal/security checkboxes are tracked.

4) Dependencies / blockers
- HealthGrid to confirm data handling constraints (PII redaction approach) and provide sample set by EOD 8/17.
- VPC peering or a short-lived test token for our private test harness for realistic egress patterns.
- Signed NDA/data handling note (Sara requested a short note on encryption & retention).

5) Target dates
- HealthGrid provides prompt set & sample conversations: target 2026-08-17
- Redwood completes initial benchmark & summary: target 2026-08-24
- MAP milestone acceptance (mutual sign-off): target 2026-08-31

Attachments: I attached an initial MAP spreadsheet (HealthGrid_MAP_v1.xlsx) that maps milestones -> owners -> acceptance criteria. Also linked a live copy of the MAP in Drive below.

Ask: Can you confirm owners for the prompt set and whether 8/31 works for milestone acceptance? If HealthGrid needs an extra week we can adjust — call out constraints.

—
Neha Kapoor

Quick engineering readout / constraints: 

- Model shortlist: I agree with the proposed three variants. Recommend running: RW-1-13B-opt (int8 path), Llama3-7B-q4f16, Mistral-7B-8bit. We should also capture a smaller 3B run if HealthGrid wants very low-cost baseline.

- Benchmark success criteria (concrete):
  * Latency (128-token completion): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms (measured on Dedicated GPU pool with steady-state traffic).
  * Throughput: sustained 25 qps with <5% tail latency variance across 30m window.
  * Quality: pass rates per HealthGrid "Critical" list >= 92% on the provided 150 prompts.
  * Cost: baseline target <= $0.03 per 1k tokens; record realized token cost (incl. cache/warmup) in the report.

- Test harness & infra: we can run in HealthGrid's environment if they provide either (a) VPC peering & a service account or (b) a short-lived test token + sample endpoint. Without peering, results may differ from production network conditions — flagging as risk.

- Data needs: representative CSV + 100 live example conversations; if any PII, we will redact locally and document retention. We'll send a short data handling note for signature.

- Engineering attachments: eval_runbook.md (run steps, scripts, metrics to collect), and a cost estimate doc. I'll attach the runbook to the MAP.

Blockers: HealthGrid's procurement timing (if PO not in place by test window we can still run a prototype but will defer final acceptance until PO).

I'll own the benchmark runs with Rishi's help for model config and quantization knobs. Expect an initial benchmark report ~7 business days after we receive the prompt set + test creds.

—
Aditya Rao
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
